options.text: It owned every oil well in the country
options.misconception: The caption says largest refiner, not owner of every well.

options.text: It was the largest oil refiner in the country
It had been broken up by the courts
options.misconception: The courts broke Standard Oil up in 1911, not by 1880.

options.text: It sold oil only in Cleveland
options.misconception: Cleveland was its base, not its only market.

rationales.A: The caption says Standard Oil was the largest refiner, not that it owned every well.
rationales.B: The caption says Rockefeller “had built Standard Oil into the largest oil-refining business in the country, refining far more oil than any rival” by 1880.
rationales.C: No court had broken Standard Oil up by 1880; the breakup came in 1911.
rationales.D: The caption says Rockefeller built the business “from his Cleveland base” — Cleveland was the base, not the only place it sold oil.
rationales.general:
Start with what the caption states, not what you know.
1. The portrait shows Rockefeller in 1880, photographed by Sarony.
2. By then he had built Standard Oil into the largest oil-refining business in the country.
3. It refined “far more oil than any rival.”
4. So by 1880 Rockefeller stood at the head of the biggest refining business in America.
Remember: a caption's superlative is the answer's core.
